benefit.name: Medical Transportation Supplement
benefit.amount: May pay $0.36 per kilometre by private vehicle, plus bus, ferry, air or train fares, accommodation for overnight travel, and travel escort costs if required
benefit.summary: Helps pay for extraordinary transportation costs to and from essential medical treatment, using the least expensive appropriate transportation.

items: You are on income assistance in the Persons with Persistent Multiple Barriers category.
You receive income assistance and reside in a special care facility.
You are on Medical Services Only.
You receive Transitional Health Services after income assistance in the PPMB category.
You receive Transitional Health Services after income assistance while residing in a special care facility.
You are a person or child approved as facing a life-threatening health need, with a direct and immediate life-threatening need for medical transportation.
You are a child in a family receiving income assistance, disability assistance, hardship assistance, MSO or Transitional Health Services.
eligibility.note: The supplement is not available if you are only receiving income assistance.

benefit.requiresNote: You may be eligible through disability assistance; income assistance in PPMB; income assistance while residing in a special care facility; or Medical Services Only. Other routes are Transitional Health Services after income assistance in PPMB or while residing in a special care facility; a person or child approved as facing a life-threatening health need with a direct and immediate life-threatening need for medical transportation; or a child in a family receiving income assistance, disability assistance, hardship assistance, MSO or Transitional Health Services. Only receiving income assistance is not a route on its own. You do not have resources available to cover your medical transportation costs.
benefit.note: Ask for pre-approval before you travel. In exceptional circumstances where you could not get funding beforehand, the ministry can consider a request afterwards, but do not count on it. Ambulance bills and the cost to buy, maintain, repair or insure a vehicle are not covered. Trips for non-essential services are not covered either.

detail.about: Helps pay for extraordinary transportation costs to and from essential medical treatment. Essential treatment means services under the Medicare Protection Act or Hospital Insurance Act with a medical practitioner, nurse practitioner, specialist or hospital. Meal allowances are normally not provided; in exceptional circumstances the ministry may issue up to $8 per meal. Travel escort costs may be paid if required. Costs may only be considered when accompanying a child under 19 or an adult incapable of travelling alone due to verified medical reasons.

aboutList.lead: Helps pay for extraordinary transportation costs to and from essential medical treatment. Essential treatment means services under the Medicare Protection Act or Hospital Insurance Act with a medical practitioner, nurse practitioner, specialist or hospital.
items: Meal allowances are normally not provided; in exceptional circumstances the ministry may issue up to $8 per meal.
Travel escort costs may be paid if required.
Costs may only be considered when accompanying a child under 19 or an adult incapable of travelling alone due to verified medical reasons.

steps: Ask for pre-approval before booking travel through My Self Serve, by phone, mail, fax or at a ministry office
Complete the medical transportation request form HR3320
Attach proof of the treatment and appointment, such as a provider note, appointment card, email, screenshot or Travel Assistance Program form
Explain the least expensive appropriate travel method and whether an escort or overnight stay is medically required
Keep approval and travel receipts in case the ministry requests them
documents: Proof of the medical appointment and why the treatment is essential
Travel dates, destination, distance and expected fare or accommodation cost
Medical confirmation that an escort or special travel method is required, if applicable
tips: Request approval before you travel; after-the-fact payment is limited to exceptional circumstances
For repeated treatment, ask whether approval can cover ongoing trips for up to 12 months
The ministry chooses the least expensive appropriate transportation, so explain accessibility or medical barriers clearly
